## PubMed strategy

The one-line query is saved in [final_strategy.txt](C:/Users/aaron/AppData/Local/Temp/psb-evals/run-05063212dadf5296/lean-optimal-codex-noseed-20260927T143906Z/final_strategy.txt).

It combines rotator-cuff terms with cellular and biologic augmentation terms, including PRP, mesenchymal cells, bone-marrow concentrate, and adipose- and tendon-derived cells. It applies the requested publication-date range through **2020-05-15**. I left out outcome, comparator, human, and study-design blocks to avoid reducing sensitivity; screening should apply those eligibility criteria.

## Checks and limits

- MeSH lookups and descriptor/tree checks covered rotator-cuff injuries; mesenchymal stem cells and their transplantation; cell- and tissue-based therapy; PRP; and platelet-rich fibrin. BMAC and bone-marrow aspirate/concentrate searches returned no dedicated descriptor. Stromal vascular fraction was checked, but its descriptor was introduced after the cutoff; its text terms are included instead.
- The final query returned **600 records** in PubMed testing. A sampled record included a 2020 randomized trial of bone-marrow concentrate and platelet products for rotator-cuff tears. No seed articles were provided, so seed validation was not possible.
- The search is intentionally broad and will retrieve animal, review, and other ineligible records for screening. The long query exceeded the bundled CLI’s GET URL limit, so I validated it through NCBI E-utilities POST and checked its query translation.

This is a draft strategy. Per PRESS, have a second information specialist peer review it before using it as the final systematic-review search.
